conviction_note: No company-level unpriced number found. The evidence is peer and counterparty proxies that point both ways (WW's clinical subscribers fell quarter on quarter; Novo's US Wegovy pill volumes grew), plus arithmetic on the full-year EBITDA guide, which has to step up in Q4 on a name that cut that guide twice in 2026. That leans mildly negative, and positioning offsets it: about 26-31% of float short, the stock down 24% in 20 days, calls bid over puts. So p_up 48 on an abs move of 15 (implied 13.7, median past reaction 12.4) gives -0.6. The findings sum to -0.4. The two numbers agree in sign and size, and both are close to a non-result.
bar: Q3 revenue consensus about $893m. Two agreeing sources: Benzinga $892.7m (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HIMS/earnings-forecasts) and TIKR about $893m (https://www.tikr.com/blog/hims-hers-stock-has-barely-moved-since-its-biggest-mens-health-launch-heres-what-november-9-has-to-show, 2026-10-23). It sits inside the company guide of revenue $880-900m and adj. EBITDA $75-95m (Q2 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001773751/000177375126000161/hims-20260630x8xkearningsr.htm). The EPS consensus is disputed ($0.06 / $0.07 / $0.09 across aggregators), so no finding is sized on EPS. No sourced adj. EBITDA consensus was found, so the company guide is the EBITDA bar.
positioning_check: Short interest: 63.37m shares, 31.5% of float, 2.5 days to cover on 2026-05-15 (MarketBeat https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/HIMS/short-interest/); 61.2m, about 26% of float, 3.2 days on 2026-07-10 (Equibles https://equibles.com/stocks/hims/shortinterest); 58.7m, 4.5 days on 2026-08-14 (Curved Trading, snippet only, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/hims/short-interest/). No October or November settlement found. This is a crowded short. Baseline skew_25d is -14.56 vol points: the market pays more for upside calls than for puts ('upside paid'). Put/call OI is 0.32. The event-implied move is 13.72%. Run-up: -23.78% over 20 days and -7.47% over 5 days, and the stock was down about 7% intraday on the print day (MarketBeat 2026-11-09) with no stated cause. Six of the last seven reactions were negative (median abs 12.36%).

findings.finding: WW International's Q3 2026 release (5 Nov) shows clinical (GLP-1 telehealth) subscribers falling from 197k at the start of Q3 to 174k at the end, a net loss of about 23k (-12% q/q), though still +40% y/y. This is a peer read that telehealth GLP-1 retention or acquisition weakened in Q3 2026, the quarter HIMS reports. HIMS's own Q2 subscribers were 2.891m, and weight loss is its largest growth driver.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Subscriber and weight-loss lines drove the Q1 2026 (-14.1%) and Q2 2025 (-12.36%) reactions per the baseline. Q2 2026 subscribers +19% y/y with a revenue beat still saw -3.97%.
findings.why_not_priced: Released four days ago by a small-cap peer. HIMS previews do not cite it, and the HIMS consensus revenue ($893m) still sits in the upper half of the guide. If the market had transmitted this, the revenue bar would have drifted toward the bottom of the guide. A -24% 20-day run-up may already partly reflect sector worry.
findings.independence: Proxy only. WW is a different business model (behavioural plus clinical) and much smaller. HIMS has not confirmed this. Novo's Q3 data (separate finding) points the other way on branded-channel volume.

findings.finding: Novo Nordisk's Q3 2026 6-K (4 Nov) reports about 3.6m US Wegovy pill prescriptions in Q3 (more than 8m since the 5 Jan launch) and combined US Wegovy +21% at CER in Q3. About 35% of 4.1m injectable Wegovy prescriptions went through the self-pay channel, which includes telehealth; HIMS sells these under its March 2026 Novo agreement. Novo also cites lower realised prices.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Branded GLP-1 mix is the stated driver of the gross-margin compression that sold the Q2 2026 print (-3.97%) despite revenue $753m vs about $695m expected. More branded volume helps revenue but has hurt the margin line.
findings.why_not_priced: Counterparty data released after HIMS last spoke (10 Aug). Novo does not name HIMS, so desks may not map it to HIMS. If it were priced, HIMS would not have fallen about 20% since 22 Oct while its main supplier's US self-pay volume grew.
findings.independence: Direct counterparty, but transmission to HIMS is not confirmed: Novo refers only to 'multiple telehealth organisations'. It conflicts with the WW peer data above. Lower realised prices cut against HIMS revenue per subscriber.

findings.finding: The full-year guide needs a large Q4 EBITDA step-up. FY26 adj. EBITDA guide $275-325m, minus H1 actuals ($44.3m Q1 + $60.3m Q2 = $104.6m), minus the Q3 guide midpoint ($85m), implies Q4 adj. EBITDA of about $85-135m. That is a 9-13% margin against 8% in Q2. Gross margin fell from 76% to 64% y/y, and management said it will stay below historical levels through H2. The FY EBITDA top end has already been cut twice in 2026 ($350m to $325m in Aug). A third trim, or a Q4 implied below the street, is the line this stock has traded on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: EBITDA and margin miss plus weak outlook, -14.1%. Q2 2026: EPS miss and gross margin down with FY EBITDA top end cut, -3.97%. Q4 2024 (Feb 2025): guide, -22.32%. Q2 2025: -12.36%.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, but no preview found states the implied Q4 EBITDA. The street focuses on Q3 revenue of about $893m. Against that, the -24% 20-day run-up and the stock trading 43% below its 52-week high suggest some of this is priced. If it were fully priced, call skew would not be bid over puts.
findings.independence: Q1 and Q1/Q2 release figures (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001773751/000177375126000074/hims-20260331x8xkearningsr.htm). Management's 'meaningful step-up in adjusted EBITDA dollars in the second half' (Q2 call, https://www.webull.com/news/15420770610291712) argues the step-up is planned, which is why this is small and not large.

findings.finding: Q3 cash flow is a test of a stated promise. Q2 operating cash flow was -$35.9m and FCF -$68.2m, driven by receivables rising from $32.1m to $375.3m. Of that, $347.4m is manufacturer discount and rebate receivables under vendor supply agreements, per the Q2 10-Q. Management said it expects to 'resume free cash flow generation in the second half' and set up a $400m receivables facility.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior reaction on the cash-flow line alone. Q2 2026 negative OCF coincided with -3.97%.
findings.why_not_priced: The receivables composition (manufacturer rebates, about $347m) is in the 10-Q body, not the press release. If the market priced a working-capital trap, preview coverage would cite cash flow. None found does.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 filings with the guidance finding, but this is a different line (cash, not EBITDA). The receivables facility funds a visible branded-GLP-1 ramp (Q3 revenue guide +47-50% y/y), so per the financing rule this is near zero, not a distress signal.

findings.finding: The Eucalyptus acquisition carries $683.9m of deferred payments in six quarterly instalments through 18 months after the June 2026 close, partly payable in Class A shares (capped at 19.9%). Of that, $537.4m is current, plus $163m of earn-outs, against $841m of cash and short-term investments and $1.365bn of convertible notes (Q2 10-Q). The Q3 call is the first update on how instalments are settled.
findings.why_not_priced: Buried in the 10-Q notes. If share settlement were in focus, the dilution would appear in previews. What the money buys is visible: international revenue of $131.4m in Q2 against a target of at least $600m for 2026. So the financing funds a ramp, and the size is small.
findings.independence: Same 10-Q as the cash-flow finding, different line (acquisition consideration, not receivables).

findings.finding: Positioning is crowded into the print: short interest about 26-31% of float (31.5% on 2026-05-15, 58.7m shares and 4.5 days to cover on 2026-08-14), stock -23.8% over 20 days and about -7% on the print day with no stated cause, 25-delta skew -14.6 vol points (calls bid), put/call OI 0.32. Any non-negative guide has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: High short interest has not stopped six of seven prints falling (baseline). The one up print, May 2025, was +18.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price: it lowers the bar rather than adding information. It is filed because the pre-print drawdown plus crowded short changes the asymmetry. If the option market saw a symmetric event, skew would not be -14.6.
findings.independence: Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/hims/shortinterest) gives 61.2m shares, 3.2 days on 2026-07-10. The baseline skew and run-up are a separate source.

findings.finding: On 21 Oct HIMS launched injectable and oral testosterone replacement, its largest men's-health expansion. The CFO has framed testosterone as the next US specialty to reach a $100m annual run rate, under 3% of next-12-month revenue (TIKR, 2026-10-23). It can be included in the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock was flat on the launch day (closed unchanged at $29.21 on 2026-10-21).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock did not move on the launch. The first early-uptake number arrives on the call. It is small relative to revenue.

findings.finding: Revenue likely prints near or above the top of the $880-900m guide. Q2 revenue of $753.2m beat a $680-700m guide and an about $695-722m consensus, though Eucalyptus (about $40m, closed in June) explains most of that. Q3 includes a full quarter of Eucalyptus already in the guide. The street is at about $893m, inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: about 8% revenue beat with FY revenue guide raised, stock -3.97%. This name sells revenue beats.
findings.why_not_priced: A modest beat inside or just above the guide is what the company told the market to expect. That is why the size is near zero.
findings.independence: Benzinga consensus $892.7m (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HIMS/earnings-forecasts). Shares the Q2 8-K with the guidance finding, on a different line (revenue, not EBITDA).

findings.finding: Insiders sold 133,905 shares (about $3.83m) in the last quarter, all under 10b5-1 plans, most recently 3,462 shares on 28 Oct at $27.60. EDGAR shows a steady run of Form 144s and Form 4s from Aug to Oct 2026 and no open-market buys.
findings.why_not_priced: Routine pre-planned sales. Close to no information, filed for completeness.

outside_window.finding: LifeMD, a telehealth weight-management peer, moved its Q3 2026 release from 9 Nov before the open to 12 Nov at 16:30 ET (press release 6 Nov, reason not retrievable). Its content lands after the HIMS window.

The DEA telemedicine special-registration final rule has been at OIRA since 2026-08-25. Temporary flexibilities for telehealth prescribing of Schedule III drugs (testosterone) expire 2026-12-31. Publication date unknown and likely after the window, unless management comments on the call.
The HHS/FDA peptide compounding interim access policy went to White House review on 14 Oct 2026. HIMS plans NAD+, sermorelin and glutathione by year end, pending final FDA rulemaking.

baseline_tension: The mild negative lean (peer subscribers down, the Q4 EBITDA step-up needed) agrees with the -24% run-up and the name's 6-of-7 down reaction history. It cuts against the option market, which pays for upside (skew -14.6), and against a 26-31% short float. p_up is held near 50 for that reason.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, sign against upside skew): the WW peer negative shrank from -1.0 to -0.7 and the Q4 EBITDA guide negative from -1.5 to -1.2; p_up moved from 47 to 48.
Lesson 5 (proxy smaller than a company number): the Novo counterparty positive was trimmed from +0.8 to +0.6 because Novo does not name HIMS.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the receivables facility funds a visible branded ramp, so the cash-flow finding went from -0.5 to -0.3. The Eucalyptus deferred-consideration item buys a closed acquisition growing international revenue, so it went from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold a 8% revenue beat at -3.97%): the revenue-beat finding went from +0.5 to +0.3.

Lesson 6 (bar): revenue bar is confirmed by two agreeing sources inside the company guide. EPS is disputed, so no EPS finding was sized. Nothing moved outside the window beyond what was already in outside_window.
Positioning (+1.0), testosterone (+0.2) and insider sales (-0.1) unchanged.
